IAEA experts reach Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant

A team of experts from the International Atomic Energy Agency arrived at the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant in southern Ukraine on Thursday, after a delay caused by shelling near the facility, the agency's director general said.

Rafael Grossi, who led the mission, told reporters that the physical integrity of the plant had been violated several times and that the agency would keep a continued presence at the site to monitor the situation closely.

The plant, the largest in Europe, has been held by Russian forces since March. Ukraine and Russia have repeatedly accused each other of shelling the area around the reactors, raising fears of a radiation accident.

Grossi said inspectors would assess damage to the buildings, check the working conditions of the Ukrainian staff operating the plant and evaluate the cooling and backup power systems in the coming days.
